newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP eyes new iron ore plant capacity lift.
newsitem.headline: BHP eyes new iron ore plant capacity lift.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Tuesday a construction of new plant producing iron bricks in Port Hedland, Western Australia is due for completion in 12 months and could operate above design capacity.

"We have a guaranteed design capacity of two million tonnes, but we believe we can achieve 2.5 million tonnes or even higher with process optimisation and de-bottlenecking over time," Geoff Wedlock, executive vice president of BHP's iron ore division told a minerals conference.
The bricks, known as hot briquetted iron, are used in the steelmaking process as raw feed.
The plant is being designed to allow for further expansion up to around five million tonnes a year, Wedlock said.
"We have not made the decision to go ahead with this yet," he said.
Wedlock said the plant would be the largest of its kind in the world.
